claims.quote: Total costs were $490K for the month, up 16%.
claims.why: All accounts went from $421,635.60 to $490,144.20: +$68,508.60, +16.2%. No cause is stated.

claims.quote: Materials were up $54K, primarily the three rooftop units for Mercy Ridge, partly offset by the copper return credit.
claims.why: Job materials went from $109,966.09 to $164,277.44: +$54,311.35. The three 25-ton RTUs for Job 2417 (Mercy Ridge) are $86,400, more than the whole change; offsets are the $6,850 copper return credit and August's $22,000 bulk copper order not repeating. Memo says 'RTUs', not 'rooftop units'.

claims.quote: Subcontractor costs fell ~$30K as the August insulation accrual reversed.
claims.why: Subcontractors went from $80,000.00 to $50,450.00: -$29,550.00, so the amount is right. The -$18,000 reversal of August's insulation accrual is offset by the actual invoice for that work ($19,250) and September's own accrual ($17,500): Rocky Mountain Insulation's net change is +$750. The fall is Front Range Sheet Metal finishing the Belmar ductwork ($41,000 -> $9,200, -$31,800).
claims.share_note: The cause is the insulation accrual, so its transactions are the whole accrual cycle (accrue, reverse, bill, re-accrue), not the reversal line alone, which by itself is 61% of the change.

claims.quote: Field labor rose about 5% on overtime to hit the Mercy Ridge set date.
claims.why: Field labor went from $156,903.20 to $164,425.27: +$7,522.07, +4.8%. The two 'OT premium - Mercy Ridge set' lines are $7,500, 99.7% of the change.

claims.quote: Equipment rental rose ~$10K on the crane pick at Mercy Ridge; a second pick is scheduled for October.
claims.why: Equipment rental went from $4,200.00 to $14,420.00: +$10,220.00. The Summit Crane pick for the RTUs ($9,800, memo 'Job 2417', not 'Mercy Ridge') is 96%.

claims.quote: Fuel rose $3.5K on higher diesel prices.
claims.why: Fuel went from $9,160.00 to $9,760.00: +$600.00, not $3.5K (more than five times too high).

claims.quote: Vehicle repairs rose $6.9K, mostly the transmission rebuild on Truck 14 (reclassed out of small tools)
claims.why: Vehicle repairs went from $819.40 to $7,753.24: +$6,933.84. The Truck 14 transmission rebuild ($6,850) was keyed to Small Tools on the vendor invoice and moved here by a reclass journal: 99% of the change. Memo says 'trans rebuild'.
Small tools went from $2,960.49 to $1,846.71: -$1,113.78. The $6,850 rebuild booked here and reclassed out nets to zero. Second claim in a two-claim sentence; no cause.

claims.quote: Permits and inspections were up $2.2K, the Mercy Ridge mechanical permit.
claims.why: Permits went from $2,200.00 to $4,400.00: +$2,200.00, so the amount is right. The Mercy Ridge mechanical permit ($1,900) was pulled in August, the prior period. September's increase is the Cherry Creek Lofts plumbing permits ($2,350) and Belmar backflow certifications ($1,600).

claims.quote: Insurance jumped $11.3K on the workers' comp audit true-up for the 2025-26 policy year.
claims.why: Insurance went from $13,200.00 to $24,500.00: +$11,300.00. The Front Range Mutual 'WC final audit 25-26 - additional premium' is exactly the change. Memo abbreviates workers' comp and the policy year.

claims.quote: Safety & training up $5.3K for the foremen's OSHA 30 class.
claims.why: Safety & training went from $650.00 to $5,950.00: +$5,300.00, so the amount is right. The OSHA 30 class is $2,100, 40% of it; the larger part is eight fall-protection kits ($3,200).

non_claims.quote: Mercy Ridge is now 38% complete and backlog stands at $6.2M.
non_claims.why: Percent complete and backlog are not ledger accounts.
